subtopics.title: Charge, the Coulomb, and the Statement of the Law

questions.question: Coulomb's law states that the force between two point charges is:
options: Proportional to the sum of the charges and inversely proportional to the distance
Proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them
Proportional to the square of the charges and independent of distance
Constant for all pairs of charges

questions.question: Charges of +2 μC and −3 μC are held 0,1 m apart. The force between them is:
A sphere carries a charge of −3,2 × 10⁻⁶ C. The number of excess electrons on it is:
When substituting into Coulomb's law you should use:
options: The signed values of the charges, so the force comes out negative for attraction
Only the larger of the two charges
The magnitudes of the charges only, deciding attraction or repulsion separately from the signs

subtopics.title: Three Charges in a Straight Line

questions.question: To find the net force on the middle of three charges in a line, you must:
options: Calculate the force from each neighbour separately, draw the two directions, then add as vectors
Add the two neighbouring charges first and do one calculation
Use the distance between the two outer charges
Ignore the smaller of the two neighbours

questions.question: B (+1 μC) lies 0,3 m right of A (+2 μC). The force of A on B is 0,2 N. Its direction is:
options: To the left, toward A, because A is bigger
To the right, away from A, because like charges repel
Zero, because B is smaller than A

questions.question: B (+1 μC) also feels C (−3 μC) sitting 0,2 m to its right. That force is:
options: 0,675 N to the left, away from C
0,675 N to the right, toward C, because unlike charges attract

questions.question: With 0,2 N rightward from A and 0,675 N rightward from C, the net force on B is:

subtopics.title: Charges at Right Angles — Coulomb's Law in Two Dimensions

questions.question: Two perpendicular forces of 0,6 N south and 0,45 N east act on a charge. The magnitude of the resultant is:
For that same resultant, the angle south of east is found from:
options: cos θ = 0,6 ÷ 0,75 with θ measured from north

questions.question: A positive charge at a corner is repelled southward by a charge due north of it. This is because the northern charge is:
Forces from two different neighbours on the same charge may be combined with Pythagoras only when:
options: The charges all have the same sign
The forces are equal in magnitude
The two forces are perpendicular to each other

subtopics.title: Touching Spheres and the Exam Traps

questions.question: Identical conducting spheres carrying +6 μC and −2 μC touch and are separated. Each sphere now carries:
After touching, the force between those two spheres at 0,1 m is:
A distance given as 5 cm must enter Coulomb's law as:
options: 5, since the constant fixes the units

questions.question: If the distance between two charges is halved and both charges are unchanged, the force:
options: Becomes a quarter of the original

questions.question: When a jersey is rubbed over your hair, objects become charged because:
options: Protons jump from the hair to the jersey
New charge is created by the friction
Electrons move from one surface to the other — charge is transferred, never created

questions.question: The strands of rubbed hair lift away from each other because:
options: Each strand carries the same kind of charge, and like charges repel
The strands are attracted to the ceiling
Warm air rises and lifts them

questions.question: Real charged objects usually carry microcoulombs because:
options: The coulomb is a very small unit
One coulomb is an enormous amount of charge, so everyday processes move only tiny fractions of it
Electrons are too heavy to move in large numbers

questions.question: Coulomb's law and Newton's law of gravitation share the same structure because both:
options: Multiply two quantities on top and divide by the distance squared

questions.question: One real difference between the electric force and gravity is that:
options: The electric force can attract or repel, while gravity only attracts
Gravity depends on distance but the electric force does not
The electric force ignores the distance squared rule
Gravity is always the stronger of the two

questions.question: A rubbed balloon holding a piece of paper up shows that:
options: The paper has lost its weight
Gravity does not act on charged objects
The balloon's charge cancels the Earth's gravity everywhere
The electric force on the paper easily beats the gravitational pull of the entire Earth on it

questions.question: In a Coulomb calculation, the signs of the charges are used to determine:
options: Whether the force is attractive or repulsive — nothing else
The value of the constant k

subtopics.title: The Tug-of-War on the Middle Charge

questions.question: The first step in any middle-charge problem should be:
options: Substituting all three charges into one formula
Drawing an arrow for the force from each neighbour, decided by attraction or repulsion
Calculating the average of the charges

questions.question: If the two arrows on the middle charge point in opposite directions, the forces:
options: Fight — subtract them, and the bigger one sets the direction

questions.question: Each neighbour's force on the middle charge is calculated using:
options: That neighbour's own distance to the middle charge
The distance between the two outer charges
The average of the two distances
Whichever distance gives the bigger force

questions.question: When the two forces on a charge are 0,45 N east and 0,6 N north, the combined force is:
options: 0,75 N, along the diagonal, by Pythagoras
